_doc: Extensible condition registry. Add entries here to support new conditions without code changes.
_medicine_classes_doc: What a medicine is, by name pattern (first matches win, all matching classes are listed). Shown with each medicine in the review evidence so the model never has to guess what a medicine is for.
_class_treats_doc: A medicine of this class is a specific treatment for the condition (used with resolved classes, so any brand counts).
_max_daily_dose_doc: Usual adult maximum daily oral dose (mg). Checked only when the strength is written on the medicine and the regimen is a morning-noon-night count (1-0-1); topical forms are skipped.
_red_flag_symptoms_doc: Symptoms that can have a cardiac cause; flagged when the patient has a cardiovascular risk condition or is 50 or older.

red_flag_symptoms.title: Possibly cardiac symptoms with cardiovascular risk

_chronic_treatment_doc: Conditions whose own medicines are expected on later prescriptions; a gap is flagged when they stop appearing.
_long_standing_doc: Long-standing conditions without a monitored medicine: listed as active once diagnosed at any visit (with chronic_treatment_conditions, cardiometabolic_conditions and control_labs).
_indication_required_doc: Conditions whose specific medicines are rarely given for anything else; such a medicine with the condition nowhere in the record is flagged. Ingredients with common other uses are excepted.
_persistent_red_flags_doc: Lesions, bleeding or weight loss lasting weeks in an adult: a serious cause has to be excluded.

persistent_red_flags.title: Persistent ulcer / lump / bleeding
persistent_red_flags.significance: Present for weeks or longer; a lesion, bleeding or weight loss that persists needs evaluation to exclude a serious cause.

_nsaid_repeat_doc: Repeated oral NSAIDs: an oral NSAID prescribed on at least min_visit_days different visit days (several encounters on one date count once), in a patient with one of nsaid_risk_conditions. Level high when the patient has at least high_when_conditions_at_least of those conditions, else medium. Days with a prescription, not days of intake. Shown to the doctor as the rule threshold on the concern.
_medicine_safety_rules_doc: Painkiller safety rules from published guidance (medicine_safety.py). Every threshold comes from the named source; where the source gives no number (Beers 'chronic'), the rule says so and uses the local nsaid_repeat threshold. Each rule is draft until a clinician verifies it (verified, verified_by, verified_on): the concern always shows its threshold, source and whether it is verified. Types: combo (two medicine groups on the same day or with overlapping courses), with_conditions (a medicine with a listed condition), daily_dose_with_conditions (an ingredient's daily dose above a limit with a listed condition), repeat_without_tests (repeated use with no listed test or BP in the record), age_repeat (repeated use at or above an age), lab_below (a medicine while a lab value is below a limit), age_dose (daily dose above a limit above an age), age_without_lab (a medicine at or above an age with no listed lab), dose_with_risk (daily dose above a limit with a risk factor). A medicine matches by its registry class, route, ingredients or name pattern.

medicine_safety_rules.title: Oral NSAID with an antiplatelet, anticoagulant or steroid
medicine_safety_rules.threshold: any oral NSAID on the same day as, or during a course of, an antiplatelet (e.g. aspirin), anticoagulant or oral steroid; even short-term use
medicine_safety_rules.significance: Raises the risk of stomach bleeding; the guideline advises avoiding even short-term use of the combination.
medicine_safety_rules.source: AGS Beers Criteria 2023 (J Am Geriatr Soc 2023;71:2052)

medicine_safety_rules.title: Diclofenac / etoricoxib with cardiovascular risk
medicine_safety_rules.threshold: diclofenac or etoricoxib (any dose) in a patient with hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidaemia, coronary disease or heart failure
medicine_safety_rules.significance: These NSAIDs carry the higher cardiovascular risk; the guidance advises avoiding them when cardiovascular risk factors are present.

medicine_safety_rules.title: High-dose ibuprofen with cardiovascular risk
medicine_safety_rules.threshold: ibuprofen above 2400 mg/day in a patient with a cardiovascular risk factor
medicine_safety_rules.significance: High-dose ibuprofen carries a cardiovascular risk similar to diclofenac.

medicine_safety_rules.title: Repeated oral NSAIDs with no kidney function or BP check
medicine_safety_rules.threshold: oral NSAID on {min_visit_days}+ visit days with no creatinine / eGFR result or no BP reading in the record (the guidance gives no visit count: the local repeat threshold is used)
medicine_safety_rules.significance: Baseline BP, kidney function and blood count are advised for continued NSAID use, then periodic review.
medicine_safety_rules.source: NICE CKS: NSAIDs - prescribing issues (2024); SPS NSAID monitoring

medicine_safety_rules.title: Repeated oral NSAIDs in an adult aged 65 or over
medicine_safety_rules.threshold: age 65+ with an oral NSAID on {min_visit_days}+ visit days (Beers says 'avoid chronic use' without a day count: the local repeat threshold is used)
medicine_safety_rules.significance: Chronic NSAID use in older adults raises the risk of GI bleeding, kidney injury and raised BP; topical NSAIDs or paracetamol are preferred.

medicine_safety_rules.title: Oral NSAID with eGFR below 30
medicine_safety_rules.threshold: any oral NSAID while the latest eGFR is below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2
medicine_safety_rules.significance: NSAIDs should be avoided in advanced kidney disease (ICMR CKD workflow: do not use NSAIDs).
medicine_safety_rules.source: KDIGO 2024 CKD guideline (NKF algorithm); ICMR STW Chronic Kidney Disease

medicine_safety_rules.title: Tramadol above 300 mg/day over age 75
medicine_safety_rules.threshold: tramadol above 300 mg/day in a patient older than 75 (adult maximum 400 mg/day)
medicine_safety_rules.significance: Older patients clear tramadol more slowly; the label caps the dose at 300 mg/day over 75.

medicine_safety_rules.title: Opioid painkiller with a benzodiazepine
medicine_safety_rules.threshold: tramadol / tapentadol on the same day as, or during a course of, a benzodiazepine (or zolpidem)
medicine_safety_rules.significance: The combination can cause severe sedation and respiratory depression; the guidance advises avoiding it.
medicine_safety_rules.source: AGS Beers Criteria 2023; FDA boxed warning on opioids with benzodiazepines

medicine_safety_rules.title: Opioid painkiller with pregabalin / gabapentin
medicine_safety_rules.threshold: tramadol / tapentadol on the same day as, or during a course of, pregabalin or gabapentin
medicine_safety_rules.significance: Raises the risk of sedation and respiratory depression; the guidance advises avoiding the combination except when switching between them.

medicine_safety_rules.title: Tramadol with an SSRI / SNRI
medicine_safety_rules.threshold: tramadol on the same day as, or during a course of, an SSRI or SNRI
medicine_safety_rules.significance: Risk of serotonin syndrome and seizures; with an SSRI, tramadol should be titrated slowly and kept to 300 mg/day or less.

medicine_safety_rules.title: Tramadol in an adult aged 65 or over with no sodium result
medicine_safety_rules.threshold: tramadol at age 65+ with no sodium result in the record
medicine_safety_rules.significance: Tramadol can cause low sodium (SIADH) in older adults; sodium should be checked when it is started or changed.

medicine_safety_rules.title: Paracetamol above 3 g/day with a liver-toxicity risk factor
medicine_safety_rules.threshold: paracetamol above 3 g/day with weight under 50 kg, liver disease or alcohol use (usual adult maximum 4 g/day)
medicine_safety_rules.significance: With these risk factors a maximum of about 3 g/day (or 15 mg/kg per dose) is advised.
medicine_safety_rules.source: BNF-based NHS guidance (BASL paracetamol position statement 2022)

Type 2 diabetes mellitus.title: Foot / leg wound or injury with diabetes
Type 2 diabetes mellitus.significance: Wounds on the feet or legs heal slowly in diabetes and can become infected or ulcerate.

Type 2 diabetes mellitus.title: Visual symptoms with diabetes
Type 2 diabetes mellitus.significance: Visual change in diabetes can reflect hyperglycaemia or retinopathy.

Hypertension.title: Symptoms that can accompany raised BP

Asthma / COPD.title: Recurring respiratory symptoms
Asthma / COPD.significance: Persistent symptoms may reflect incomplete control.

Thyroid disorder.title: Symptoms that can relate to thyroid status

Heart failure.title: Symptoms that can reflect fluid status
Heart failure.significance: Breathlessness or swelling in heart failure needs review.

Epilepsy.title: Seizure-type events recorded
Epilepsy.significance: Recurrent events may indicate incomplete control.

meds.note: Calcium-channel blockers are a known cause of ankle swelling.

symptom_med_links.title: Cough while on an ACE inhibitor

meds.note: ACE inhibitors are a known cause of dry cough.

symptom_med_links.title: Muscle pain while on a statin

_drug_rules_doc: Medicine duplication and interaction rules (clinical_snapshot.py). Duplicates are checked per clinical day (all encounters on one date), so two departments prescribing on the same day are caught. duplicate_classes: medicine_classes whose second same-day member adds risk, not benefit (NSAIDs counted oral only). nsaid_cumulative_days: total stated duration of oral NSAIDs across the record (one value per clinical day) from which a flag is raised. azole_long_term: an oral azole on at least min_days clinical days, or for at least min_duration_days in total, with no liver test (liver_tests: lab_catalog keys).
_expected_investigations_doc: A finding in the record that is normally followed by a test, and the record holds no such test (any date): reported as a record gap, never as advice. Each rule matches visit diagnoses / complaints by pattern (on at least min_days clinical days), or a temperature reading at or above temp_f_at_least. tests: lab_catalog keys, any one of which closes the gap.

expected_investigations.why: Urinary frequency is usually checked with a urine test (infection, sugar).
Recurrent fungal infection is a recognised presentation of raised blood glucose.
A blood count is the usual first test for a fever.
Anaemia is a common, testable cause of recurring weakness.

expected_investigations.test_label: blood glucose / HbA1c or vitamin B12
expected_investigations.why: Raised glucose and low B12 are common, testable causes of peripheral nerve symptoms.
Swelling with diabetes or hypertension is usually checked with kidney function and urine protein.

_diagnosis_refinements_doc: Groups of diagnosis names where one is a refinement or synonym of another (lichen simplex chronicus is a form of eczema). A document and a record naming members of one group are not reported as a diagnosis mismatch.
_guidelines_doc: Indian guideline context for the clinical snapshot (clinical_snapshot.guideline_context) and the AI review evidence.

Each section has a source and 'verified'. A section runs only when verified is true, or when ENABLE_DRAFT_GUIDELINES is on (testing). Set verified to true only after a clinician checks every value against the cited document.
Rows state what the record shows against the guideline; they never recommend a medicine, dose or test.
Change 'version' whenever a value changes: it is part of the review prompt version, so cached reviews regenerate.

guidelines._verification_doc: A section is verified only with verified: true, verified_by (the clinician) and verified_on (YYYY-MM-DD); set them with scripts/verify_guideline.py. Verified sections raise flags and reach the AI review and brief; draft sections are shown to the doctor and in /summary as information only.

diabetes_control.label: HbA1c
diabetes_control.source: ICMR Guidelines for Management of Type 2 Diabetes (2018)

bp_targets._lower_doc: The lower target applies when the patient has a bp_lower_target_conditions condition.
bp_targets.source: ICMR Standard Treatment Workflow: Hypertension / India Hypertension Control Initiative

monitoring._doc: Tests a condition is followed with, by lab_catalog key; due when the latest dated result is older than every_days. HbA1c for diabetes is in diabetes_control.
monitoring.source: ICMR T2DM Guidelines (2018); ICMR Standard Treatment Workflow: Hypertension

haemoglobin._doc: Anaemia thresholds by age (years), sex and pregnancy, g/dL. The first matching group applies; 'below' = anaemia threshold, bands from mildest.
haemoglobin.source: Anemia Mukt Bharat (MoHFW) / WHO haemoglobin thresholds (2011)

bmi.source: Consensus BMI cut-offs for Asian Indians (Misra et al., 2009), as used in ICMR-INDIAB

lab_context._doc: Bands for a result read against guideline cut-offs, also when the report gave no range. [from, below, label]; null = open. Not a lab status.

egfr.source: KDIGO CKD classification, as used in ICMR Standard Treatment Workflow: CKD

urine_acr.source: KDIGO CKD classification, as used in ICMR Standard Treatment Workflow: CKD

antibiotics._doc: Antibiotic at a visit whose diagnosis is only a usually-viral syndrome, with no bacterial marker in that visit's diagnosis or complaint.
antibiotics.source: ICMR Treatment Guidelines for Antimicrobial Use in Common Syndromes (2019)

tb_screening.source: National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP): presumptive TB

_symptom_combinations_doc: A symptom concept (symptom_map tags) that matters with a condition or with another symptom: flagged when any 'tags' symptom is recorded together with any 'with_conditions' or any 'with_tags' symptom anywhere in the record.

symptom_combinations.title: Possible renal/fluid cause – check creatinine, urine albumin
symptom_combinations.significance: Swelling around the eyes or face with hypertension, diabetes or leg swelling can reflect kidney disease (protein loss) or fluid retention.

_undiagnosed_lab_bands_doc: A lab result in a band that suggests a condition the record does not note (no diagnosis, complaint, long-term entry or treating medicine): flagged as 'probable', never as a diagnosis. Bands are [from, to) on the latest dated result in 'unit' (mmol/mol HbA1c is converted). treated_by_class: a medicine of this class means the condition is managed.

undiagnosed_lab_bands.label: HbA1c
undiagnosed_lab_bands.source: HbA1c: normal <5.7% (<42 mmol/mol); prediabetes 5.7-6.4% (42-47 mmol/mol); diabetes >=6.5% (>=48 mmol/mol)

bands.title: Probable prediabetes
bands.meaning: HbA1c 5.7-6.4% (42-47 mmol/mol) indicates an increased risk of developing type 2 diabetes; not noted in the record.

bands.title: Probable diabetes
bands.meaning: HbA1c 6.5% or higher (>=48 mmol/mol) supports a diagnosis of diabetes, usually confirmed with a repeat test; not noted in the record.

_symptom_medicine_risks_doc: A symptom linked to a medicine risk when the record supports it: the symptom (symptom_map tags), at least min_days of the medicine group by the given route (course windows, registry therapeutic group), and one of with_conditions. Raised only when none of 'tests' is in the record; the flag names the test to check.

symptom_medicine_risks.title: Weakness with long NSAID use and gastritis – check haemoglobin
symptom_medicine_risks.significance: Weakness after long NSAID use with gastritis can reflect slow blood loss from the stomach (anaemia).
